titulo.alumno: Common verbs in the present tense

intro: Build affirmative sentences in the present with everyday verbs and respect the V2 position.

frases.estudio: Ik woon in Utrecht en ik werk in een café.
frases.alumno: I live in Utrecht and I work in a café.

frases.estudio: Mijn broer leert Nederlands op school.
frases.alumno: My brother is learning Dutch at school.

frases.estudio: Na het werk kookt mijn broer thuis.
frases.alumno: After work my brother cooks at home.

frases.estudio: In het weekend bezoeken we onze vrienden.
frases.alumno: At the weekend we visit our friends.

texto: In Dutch, the regular present is formed with the stem for «ik» (werk, woon, kook), the stem + -t for «jij/hij/zij» (werkt, woont, kookt) and the -en form for the plurals «wij/jullie/zij» (werken, wonen, koken). If the sentence begins with an adverbial phrase of time or place («Elke dag...», «Na het werk...»), the conjugated verb must stay in second position and the subject moves after it (subject-verb inversion).

pregunta.texto: What ending does the verb stem take in the present with the subject «hij» (my brother)?

opciones.texto: You add -t to the verb stem
opciones.explicacion: «Koken» has the stem «kook», and with «mijn broer» (hij) it becomes «kookt».

opciones.texto: You add -en as in the plural
opciones.explicacion: The -en ending is reserved for the plural forms (wij, jullie, zij).

opciones.texto: You leave the bare stem with no ending
opciones.explicacion: The bare stem alone corresponds to the first person «ik».

pregunta.texto: What does the brother do after work?

frase.texto: Na het werk kookt mijn broer thuis.

opciones.explicacion: «Kookt» is cooks and «thuis» is at home.

opciones.texto: He goes to a café in Utrecht with friends.
opciones.explicacion: It confuses the brother's workplace with the activity afterwards.

opciones.texto: He learns languages at night school.
opciones.explicacion: The school study is mentioned in the previous sentence.

pregunta.texto: Complete with the correct verb form for the subject «wij».

opciones.explicacion: With the plural pronoun «wij» the verb takes the full -en form.
The -t ending is for the singular («hij oefent»).

pregunta.texto: Why does the verb «kookt» come before «mijn broer» in «Na het werk kookt mijn broer thuis»?

opciones.texto: Because starting the sentence with an adverbial phrase forces inversion
opciones.explicacion: In Dutch the finite verb always occupies the second syntactic position (the V2 rule).

opciones.texto: Because it is an indirect question
opciones.explicacion: It is not a question, but a statement with syntactic inversion.

opciones.texto: Because the subject «mijn broer» is a stressed pronoun
opciones.explicacion: The inversion depends on the structure of the sentence, not on the type of noun.

pregunta.texto: What activity do they do during the weekend?

frase.texto: In het weekend bezoeken we onze vrienden.

opciones.explicacion: «Bezoeken» means to visit and «onze vrienden» means our friends.

opciones.texto: They work together in the café.
opciones.explicacion: The text says they work on weekdays and have social time at the weekend.

opciones.texto: They stay resting in the garden.
opciones.explicacion: It does not mention resting in the garden, but visiting friends.

pregunta.texto: Complete with the verb for living in the first person.

frase.texto: Ik ___ in Utrecht en ik werk in een café.

opciones.explicacion: With «ik» the direct verb stem is used («wonen» -> «woon»).
It takes the -t of the second and third person singular («hij woont»).
It is the infinitive or the plural form («wij wonen»).

frase.texto: Na het werk kookt mijn broer thuis

piezas.traduccion: After work my brother cooks at home.
piezas.explicacion: Initial time phrase, verb in second position and inversion of the subject.
